newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Sept 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Sept 28.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Bangladesh should sell natural gas in the international market to fuel its economic development, World Bank's energy expert Per Ljung said.
Former Finance Minister and a top opposition leader Saifur Rahman said major political parties should refrain from "conventional politics" and work together to build up the nation.

Bangladesh needs $2.5 billion in private investment by the end of the decade to build up its power generation system, said a visiting World Bank official. He said foreign investors were interested to invest in Bangladesh's power sector.

Sinking of new tubewells in Dhaka city has become risky due to alarming fall in the ground water level, water supply authorities said. The water table now remains at 82 feet below the surface even after the recent heavy monsoon.
Bangladesh Foreign Minister Abdus Samad Azad has expressed Bangladesh's support for the proposed rapid deployment force headquarters to assist the UN peacekeeping operations.
The government's Pay Commission has prepared a draft national pay scale proposing raises between 50 and 65 percent in public salaries.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina celebrates her birthday on Saturday, her first in office. The celebration is lilely to be in private and quiet, and there is no known official programme on the occassion.
